editorial:
Imagine your favorite loud-mouthed prankster from the early 2000s suddenly finding out he is going to be a dad. That is exactly what happens here. You get to see Ali G wake up from a twenty-year nap of just hanging out and doing nothing, only to find out his girlfriend Julie is almost ready to pop. The vibe is pure chaos from the start. It feels like a wild road trip movie where a guy who has no clue how the real world works tries to make a quick buck in America to support his baby. It is loud, colorful, and completely ridiculous in the best way possible.

What really works is how Sacha Baron Cohen still nails the character without making it feel old. The pacing is quick, and the scenes where he clashes with serious American businessmen are gold. While some of the plot twists in the second half feel a bit random, the laughs make up for it. You should definitely watch this if you love cringe humor and big personalities. For the best experience, I suggest streaming it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video so you can see every detail of his outrageous outfits, or just grab the 4K Blu-ray if you want to keep it forever.
endingExplained: In the final act, you find out the villains were actually trying to steal Ali G's secret stash of vintage streetwear. After a huge, messy fight in Las Vegas, Ali G accidentally knocks out the bad guys while trying to dance. He manages to save his child and realizes that being a dad is more important than fame. He returns home to Julie and the baby, finally deciding to get a real job.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves cringe comedy and Sacha Baron Cohen
